contentBlocks.title: SRD R370 Monthly Review — How Your Eligibility Is Checked Every Month
contentBlocks.description: The SRD R370 grant is re-evaluated every single month — approval this month does not guarantee payment next month. Understand how SASSA's automated review works, what databases it checks against, and what triggers a decline so you can maintain your grant month after month.

contentBlocks.text: SRD R370 Monthly Review — How It Works

Unlike other SASSA grants that remain approved for extended periods, the SRD R370 grant is evaluated EVERY month. This means your eligibility is reassessed from scratch each month. Understanding how this monthly review works is the key to maintaining your grant and avoiding unexpected declines.

contentBlocks.title: Your Status Can Change Monthly
contentBlocks.text: Being approved this month does NOT guarantee approval next month. Every month is a fresh assessment. Your status can change based on bank activity, database updates, or changes in your personal circumstances.
SASSA runs an automated check against multiple government databases and your bank account at the beginning of each month:

items: Bank account scan: SASSA checks your linked bank account for any deposits exceeding R624 in the previous month
UIF database: checks if your ID is still registered as an active UIF beneficiary
NSFAS database: checks if you are listed as an active NSFAS-funded student
SARS database: checks if you are registered for PAYE tax
SASSA database: confirms you are not receiving any other social grant
Home Affairs: verifies your ID is valid and not flagged as deceased

rows: SASSA runs automated checks against all databases
Bank account audit — all linked accounts are scanned for deposits
Status updates appear on the portal (Pending, Approved, or Declined)
Payment batch preparation for approved beneficiaries
Payments are processed and sent to banks or Cash Send

contentBlocks.text: What Can Trigger a Decline During the Review

items: A friend or family member deposits money into your account — any amount above R624 total
You transfer money between your own accounts (savings to chequing counts as a deposit)
Your employer pays you a final payout or bonus
The Department of Labour still shows you as UIF-registered even though you no longer receive UIF
Your former university still shows you as an active NSFAS student
Your ID was flagged as deceased or lost in the Home Affairs system
You turned 59 and will no longer be eligible at 60

contentBlocks.text: How to Maintain Your Eligibility Month-to-Month

items: Keep bank deposits as low as possible — avoid any deposit exceeding R624 in a single month
If you must receive money, ask the sender to use Cash Send, eWallet, or another method that does not go through your bank account
Do not use your SASSA-linked bank account for business or secondary transactions
Ensure your UIF status is terminated if you are no longer receiving UIF (get a UI-19 letter)
Ensure your NSFAS status is cancelled if you have completed your studies
Check your status at the start of each month so you know immediately if you need to appeal

faqs.question: Why is the SRD grant reviewed every month but other grants are not?
faqs.answer: The SRD grant is a temporary relief measure designed for people with no income at all. Monthly reviews ensure it goes to those who genuinely need it each month, unlike permanent grants that have longer assessment periods.

faqs.question: If I was declined one month, will I be declined the next month too?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. If the reason for decline changes (e.g., a one-time bank deposit), you may be approved the following month. Each month is evaluated independently.

faqs.question: Do I need to submit documents every month?
faqs.answer: No. You only submit documents if you need to appeal a decline. The monthly review is automated using existing databases and bank scans.

faqs.question: What if I get a job mid-month? Will I lose my grant?
faqs.answer: If your employer pays you and the deposit exceeds R624, you may be declined the following month. However, you should report your employment status change to SASSA.

faqs.question: Can I prevent the monthly review from scanning my account?
faqs.answer: No. The monthly bank audit is a mandatory part of the SRD grant system. You cannot opt out of the review process while receiving the grant.

faqs.question: What happens if I miss checking my status for several months?
faqs.answer: Your status is still evaluated monthly. However, if you do not check it, you may miss an appeal deadline (90 days). Check regularly to protect your grant.
